generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and exercise science, you compare rival accounts of what improves performance or prevents injury. You take each study apart to see its claim, evidence and method; you weigh the accounts against one another; and you draw them into a conclusion of your own. The three skills run together whenever you argue from the evidence base.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport science students review the evidence on a training method. One reports each study in turn and leaves the findings unconnected. The other takes each study apart, weighs the stronger designs against the weaker ones, then argues a conclusion of their own about the method. The second review makes a case; the first only lists, and running the three skills together is the reason.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and exercise science, analysis, evaluation and synthesis work best as one practice. You take a study apart, weigh its design against others, and build a conclusion of your own from the evidence. Running the three skills together is what lets you argue from the evidence base rather than just summarise it.

check.body: A student takes an article apart into its claim and evidence, weighs it against a rival reading, then draws both into a claim of their own. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: The three critical skills working as one practice: analysis, then evaluation, then synthesis, each feeding the next.
_items.feedback: Yes. The student moved from taking the source apart, to weighing it, to building an argument.

_items.text: Only analysis, because the student began by taking the article apart.
_items.feedback: Analysis was the first move, but the student also weighed the reading and built a claim.

_items.text: Only summary, because the student used more than one source.
_items.feedback: Using sources together to build a claim is synthesis, not summary.

_items.text: Evaluation on its own, because the student compared two readings.
_items.feedback: Weighing the readings was evaluation, but it sat inside the fuller practice of all three skills.
